problem.summary: Real-time detectors must balance accuracy against compute for edge and mobile use, and it was unclear how to fold DINOv3's strong foundation features into DETR-style real-time models: DINOv3 only emits single-scale features while detection needs multi-scale ones, and deployment scales from GPU down to mobile must all be covered.
statements: Achieving a good balance between detection performance and computational efficiency remains the key challenge, especially for lightweight models meant for edge and mobile devices.

DINOv3 outputs single-scale (1/16) dense features, while objects vary widely in size and multi-scale features are among the most effective ways to improve detection, so an efficient single-to-multi-scale conversion is required.
Despite DINOv3's robust feature representations, the feasibility and effectiveness of integrating it into DETR-based real-time models had not been fully investigated.
Ultra-lightweight variants (Nano, Pico, Femto, Atto) must meet strict parameter budgets while still delivering usable accuracy.

evidence.quote: Achieving a good balance between detection performance and computational efficiency remains a key challenge, especially for lightweight models suitable for edge and mobile devices
DINOv3 is based on a ViT backbone, which naturally produces single-scale (1/16) dense features
In object detection, however, objects vary widely in size, and multiscale features are one of the most effective ways to improve performance
Despite the robust feature representations offered by DINOv3 [21] in diverse scenarios

background.summary: Builds on the authors' DEIM (Dense O2O) pipeline and the RT-DETR architecture, importing DINOv3 foundation features; prior art includes ViTDet's Feature2Pyramid for deriving multi-scale features from a plain ViT and the HGNetv2 CNN backbones used by D-FINE and the ultra-light variants.

relatedWork.name: DEIM
relatedWork.relation: the authors' prior method whose Dense O2O training DEIMv2 extends
relatedWork.quote: In our previous DEIM [7], we proposed Dense O2O, which increases the number of objects per training image to provide stronger supervision, improving convergence and performance

relatedWork.name: DINOv3
relatedWork.relation: foundation vision model providing pretrained/distilled backbones and semantics
relatedWork.quote: Despite the robust feature representations offered by DINOv3 [21] in diverse scenarios

relatedWork.name: RT-DETR
relatedWork.relation: overall architecture template DEIMv2 follows (backbone, hybrid encoder, decoder)
relatedWork.quote: Our overall architecture follows the design of RT-DETR [14]

relatedWork.name: HGNetv2
relatedWork.relation: efficient CNN backbone family used for the ultra-lightweight variants
relatedWork.quote: HGNetv2 [1], developed by the Baidu PaddlePaddle team, is widely used in realtime DETR frameworks for its efficiency

evidence.quote: ViTDet [10] introduced the Feature2Pyramid module, which generates multi-scale features from the final ViT output using deconvolution

solution.summary: DEIMv2 extends DEIM with DINOv3 features across eight model sizes: a Spatial Tuning Adapter converts DINOv3's single-scale output into multi-scale features and enhances them with a lightweight detail branch, while a simplified decoder (SwiGLU FFN, RMSNorm, shared query position embedding) and object-level CopyBlend augmentation strengthen Dense O2O; ultra-light variants instead use progressively pruned HGNetv2-B0 backbones.
solution.approach: Combine DINOv3-pretrained/distilled ViT backbones with a parameter-free Spatial Tuning Adapter for large variants, and pruned HGNetv2 CNN backbones for ultra-light variants, all on an RT-DETR-style architecture with a simplified decoder and upgraded Dense O2O matching.
components: Spatial Tuning Adapter (STA): fully convolutional network that resizes 1/16-scale features from ViT blocks (e.g. 5th, 8th, 11th) into multiple scales via parameter-free bilinear interpolation and adds a Bi-Fusion ultra-lightweight CNN detail branch
DINOv3-pretrained ViT-Small / ViT-Small+ backbones for X and L, ViT-Tiny / ViT-Tiny+ distilled from DINOv3 for M and S
Progressively depth- and width-pruned HGNetv2-B0 backbones for Nano, Pico, Femto and Atto
Simplified decoder: SwiGLU FFN and RMSNorm replacing FFN and LayerNorm, plus one position embedding shared across all decoder layers
Enhanced Dense O2O with object-level CopyBlend augmentation that blends new objects into images
Five-term weighted loss (MAL, FGL, DDF, L1 bbox, GIoU), with the local FGL/DDF losses excluded for Pico, Femto and Atto
Hybrid encoder plus iterative decoder that refines the top-K candidate boxes, following RT-DETR

evidence.quote: and introduce a Spatial Tuning Adapter (STA), which efficiently converts DINOv3’s single-scale output into multi-scale features and complements strong semantics with fine-grained details to enhance detection
we employ HGNetv2 with depth and width pruning to meet strict resource budgets
In DEIMv2, we further explore Dense O2O at the object level with Copy-Blend, which adds new objects without their backgrounds
sharing a single position embedding across all decoder layers, eliminating redundant computation

experiments.summary: Evaluates all eight DEIMv2 variants on COCO val2017 against real-time detectors (DEIM, D-FINE, RT-DETRv2, YOLOv8/9/10/11/12, Gold-YOLO) and ultra-light detectors (NanoDet-M, PicoDet, YOLOv10-N), reporting AP, parameters, GFLOPs and latency.

evidence.quote: Notably, our largest model, DEIMv2-X, achieves 57.8 AP with only 50.3M parameters, surpassing prior X- scale models that require over 60M parameters for just 56.5 AP
DEIMv2-S sets a new milestone as the first model with fewer than 10M parameters to exceed the 50 AP threshold on COCO, achieving 50.9 AP with only 11M parameters and 26 GFLOPs
Even the ultra-lightweight DEIMv2-Pico, with just 1.5M parameters, delivers 38.5 AP—matching YOLOv10-Nano (2.3M) with ∼50% fewer parameters

limitations.summary: There is no dedicated limitations section, but the authors state that latency has not been optimized, that DINOv3-driven gains concentrate on medium and large objects while small-object detection stays a challenge, and that local distillation losses hurt ultra-lightweight training.
items: Latency of the proposed models has not been optimized; techniques such as Flash Attention could further accelerate inference.
Accuracy gains over DEIM come mostly from medium and large objects; small-object detection remains a challenge across scales.
FGL and DDF local losses degrade performance of ultra-lightweight models, so they are excluded from training Pico, Femto and Atto.

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that the latency of the proposed methods has not been optimized
These results indicate that DEIMv2’s main advantage lies in enhancing the representation and detection of medium-to-large objects, whereas small-object detection remains a challenge across scales

applying FGL and DDF losses to ultra-lightweight models degrades performance. We attribute this to their limited capacity and inherently weaker baseline accuracy, which reduces the effectiveness of self-distillation

futureDirections.direction: Find better ways to integrate DINOv3 features into real-time detectors.
futureDirections.quote: Exploring ways to better integrate DINOv3 features into real-time detectors thus represents an interesting direction for future work

futureDirections.direction: Use Flash Attention and similar techniques to reduce the not-yet-optimized inference latency.
futureDirections.quote: Techniques such as Flash Attention [2], as in Yolov12 [22], could further accelerate inference

applications.quote: Real-time object detection [6, 18, 22, 29] is a critical component in many practical applications, including autonomous driving [11], robotics [16], and industrial defect detection [8]

deploymentClaims: Eight model sizes from X to Atto cover GPU, edge and mobile deployment.
DEIMv2-X reaches 57.8 AP at 13.75 ms latency with 50.3M parameters; DEIMv2-S reaches 50.9 AP with 9.71M parameters.
DEIMv2-Atto runs at 0.49M parameters and 0.76 GFLOPs; Pico matches YOLOv10-Nano with about 50% fewer parameters.

evidence.quote: DEIMv2 spans eight model sizes from X to Atto, covering GPU, edge, and mobile deployment
highlight its suitability for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices
